1	---
2	title: Share a graphic
3	description: Save a graphic as a .fjgraphic file with the fonts and pictures it uses, and bring one into another project.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A `.fjgraphic` file carries one graphic, with the fonts and pictures it uses, so you can move it to another project or give it to someone else with Frame Job. Finder calls the file a Frame Job Graphic.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
13	  where={['Export… and From File… in the Insert Graphic sheet', 'A .fjgraphic opened from the Finder']}
14	  tools={['export_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Export a graphic
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…** and pick the graphic in the Insert Graphic sheet. It can be a bundled template or one from **This Project**.
22	
23	2. Choose **Export…**. It's dimmed when the chosen graphic doesn't compile, and while another export is running.
24	
25	3. In the save panel, which slides down over the sheet with `<module>.fjgraphic` as the name, choose where to put the file and save.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	The Insert Graphic sheet stays open. The line under its lists says `Exporting <title>…`, then `Exported <title> to <file>:` followed by the files the package holds, or says why it couldn't.
30	
31	Saving over an existing file replaces it whole. If the export fails, the file already there is left as it was.
32	
33	Exporting changes nothing in the project and isn't an undo step.
34	
35	## What a package packs
36	
37	A package holds the module and only the project fonts and pictures the graphic uses. To find those, Frame Job draws the graphic and packs what it saw used:
38	
39	- Every frame with the default properties. A graphic longer than 900 frames has 900 frames spread evenly over it.
40	- Then each choice of each [Enum](/graphics/properties/#enum) property and the other value of each [Boolean](/graphics/properties/#boolean) property, one at a time, over 30 frames each. It draws at most 32 of these.
41	
42	A font is packed when the graphic drew or measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font lacks. A picture is packed when the graphic's `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are never packed, because every copy of Frame Job has them, so a bundled template's package holds its module and nothing else.
43	
44	A frame that fails to draw is skipped.
45	
46	:::caution
47	[String](/graphics/properties/#string) and [Asset](/graphics/properties/#asset) properties are only tried at their defaults. A font or picture the graphic reaches only through another value, such as a different title or another picture, isn't packed. Read the file list in the message line after an export, and if something's missing, make it that property's default in the module and export again.
48	:::
49	
50	## The .fjgraphic file
51	
52	A package is a zip with nothing compressed. It holds `manifest.json`, the module, and the `fonts/` and `assets/` folders. The manifest gives the package's format, the module, its title, category and description, the Frame Job version that wrote it, and each file's path, name, size and SHA-256.
53	
54	Exporting the same graphic twice with the same version of Frame Job gives byte-identical files.
55	
56	A file name a zip path can't hold is stored under a tidied name. That covers a `:` or `\`, a control character and a leading `.`, so `a:b.ttf` is stored as `a-b.ttf`. The manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and `asset(name)` still finds its picture.
57	
58	A package can hold at most about 4 GiB and 65,535 files.
59	
60	## Open from the Finder
61	
62	Double-click a `.fjgraphic`, open it with **Open With**, drop it on Frame Job's Dock icon, or open it from a browser's downloads. Frame Job [checks the package](#package-checks), then puts up the [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet).
63	
64	The package goes into the front project, the one whose window is in front. With no project open, it goes into a new untitled project. A package that fails its checks before the sheet appears shows an alert and opens no project.
65	
66	If Frame Job wasn't running, it opens first and the package waits until any projects it reopens are back, so it lands once, in one project, with no Welcome window.
67	
68	**File ▸ Open** doesn't list `.fjgraphic` files, and there's no menu item for importing one.
69	
70	## Import with From File…
71	
72	<Steps>
73	
74	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**. The Insert Graphic sheet closes and a file panel opens.
75	
76	2. Choose a `.fjgraphic`. The [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet) appears for that same project.
77	
78	</Steps>
79	
80	The panel also takes a `.js` module, which goes straight onto the timeline. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
81	
82	## The Import Graphic sheet
83	
84	Before anything is copied, the sheet shows the graphic's title and description, then what will happen to each file:
85	
86	| Line | What it can read |
87	| --- | --- |
88	| Module | `Module: lower-third`, `Module: lower-third (already in this project)`, or `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)` |
89	| Fonts | The font files, each plain, marked `(already here)`, or marked `(as Inter-2.ttf)`. With none, `Fonts: none`. |
90	| Pictures | The picture files, each plain or marked `(already here)`. With none, `Pictures: none`. |
91	
92	Under them it says "Importing copies these files into this project's graphics. It is not an Undo step."
93	
94	Choose **Import** to copy the files, or **Cancel** to copy nothing.
95	
96	If the project's graphics folder changed while the sheet was up and the import can't go ahead, Frame Job beeps, the sheet stays open and it says why.
97	
98	## Name clashes
99	
100	An import never replaces a file. Each file keeps the name the package gives it, unless that name is taken:
101	
102	| The project already has | What happens |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| A file of that name with the same contents | It's used as it is, and the sheet says "already here". |
105	| A different module of that name | The module is copied under a new name with `-2`, `-3` and so on: `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)`. |
106	| A different font of that name | The font is copied under a new name, such as `as Inter-2.ttf`. A font is found by its family, so its file name changes nothing. |
107	| A different picture of that name | The import stops, because the module asks for its pictures by name. An alert says so. Rename or remove the project's file and import again. |
108	
109	A name that differs only in case counts as taken. A module name also counts as taken while clips left behind by a [deleted graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/) still use it.
110	
111	To find the project's pictures, see [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
112	
113	## After an import
114	
115	**Import** copies the files into the project's graphics folder and opens the Insert Graphic sheet on **This Project** with the graphic chosen, ready to insert. The line under the lists says what happened:
116	
117	`Imported Lower third as lower-third. Added: lower-third.js, fonts/Inter.ttf. Already here: assets/logo.png.`
118	
119	An import only copies files. It places no clip, so choose **Insert** when you want one on the timeline.
120	
121	Importing isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. An untitled project keeps the files when it's first saved. If a copy fails part-way, what it had copied is removed.
122	
123	## Package checks
124	
125	Frame Job checks a package before it copies anything, and a check that fails writes nothing. The message reads `<file> cannot be imported:` followed by the reason.
126	
127	| What's wrong | What the reason says |
128	| --- | --- |
129	| The file is empty | `it is empty (0 bytes)` |
130	| It isn't a zip, or it's damaged | For example `the package is not a zip: no end of central directory record` |
131	| It was compressed, for example by zipping it again | `<entry> is compressed (method 8); a .fjgraphic holds stored entries only` |
132	| It was changed after it was written | The entry that differs from the manifest by path, size or SHA-256, such as `<entry> is 2048 bytes, but the manifest says 1024` |
133	| A newer Frame Job wrote it | `the package is format 2; this Frame Job reads format 1 — a newer Frame Job wrote it` |
134	| A font is bad | `the font "<name>" is not a .ttf or .otf file`, or why it doesn't load |
135	| A picture is bad | `the picture "<name>"` and why: it isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file, its name can't be used, or it's empty |
136	
137	A module that doesn't compile passes these checks and is imported. It's listed on **This Project** with **Export…** dimmed, and **Insert** places nothing and shows the first error. Fix it the way you'd fix any module. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
138	
139	## With an agent
140	
141	`export_graphic` is **Export…**, writing to a path instead of through a save panel, and it also says how many frames it drew and how many failed. The assistant asks you before it runs, because it can replace a file.
142	
143	`import_graphic` is **Import** without the sheet, so nothing asks first. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
144	
145	## Related
146	
147	- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
148	- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
149	- [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/)
150	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
151

1	---
2	title: The Graphic sub-tab
3	description: See which module draws a graphic clip, open it in your editor, and read what it reports when it doesn't draw as it should.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	Select a graphic clip and the inspector's **Clip** tab gains a **Graphic** sub-tab. It's where you set what the graphic shows, see which module draws it, and find out what's wrong when it doesn't draw as it should.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic" tools={['set_graphic', 'get_graphic']} />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="07-clip-graphic.inspector"
15	  alt="The Clip tab with a graphic clip selected. Graphic, Picture and Clip sub-tabs sit above four sections. Source is collapsed and reads Lower third. Properties is open with six rows: Title, subtitle, accent, size, boxed and align. Size is collapsed and reads 960 × 540, and Timeline is collapsed and reads 00:00:05:00."
16	/>
17	
18	## The Graphic sub-tab
19	
20	A graphic clip's sub-tabs are **Graphic**, **Picture** and **Clip**, in that order. **Graphic** appears only when every selected clip is a graphic clip, so any other kind of clip in the selection removes it.
21	
22	| Section | What it's for | Summary when collapsed | Starts | Shows |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| [Source](#source) | What draws the clip, and what the module reports about it | The error or warning count, or the module's name | Collapsed | Always |
25	| [Properties](/graphics/properties/) | What the graphic shows | The number of properties | Open | When every selected clip is drawn by one module |
26	| [Size](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's width and height | `W × H` | Collapsed | Always |
27	| [Timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's own timeline | Its length | Collapsed | With one clip selected |
28	
29	There's no **Color** sub-tab. To grade a graphic, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above it.
30	
31	## The Picture sub-tab
32	
33	A graphic has the same layer settings as other clips, so you can move, scale and fade it: [Transform](/canvas/transform/) (position, scale, rotation and opacity), [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/), [Shadow](/effects/shadow/), [Filters](/effects/filters/), [Reflection](/effects/reflection/), [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) and [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
34	
35	It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, which are for clips drawn from media.
36	
37	## The Clip sub-tab
38	
39	**Clip** has the clip's [Timing](/editing/timing-section/) when one clip is selected, [Transition](/motion/transition-settings/) when the clip overlaps the one before it, and [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
40	
41	There's no Speed section. A graphic has no speed control or speed ramp, because its timing comes from the module and its [Length](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
42	
43	## Source
44	
45	Source says what draws the clip. Its summary, when collapsed, is `1 error` or `2 warnings` if there's anything to report, and otherwise the module's name.
46	
47	### Name, File and Revision
48	
49	| Row | What it shows |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **Name** | The module's display name, or its file name when it has none |
52	| **File** | The module's file, `<name>.js` |
53	| **Revision** | The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the file's text, which change whenever the text does, or `missing` when the file is gone |
54	
55	### Open in Editor
56	
57	**Open in Editor** opens the module in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files. Save there and the preview redraws within a moment. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
58	
59	### Reveal in Finder
60	
61	**Reveal in Finder** shows the module's file in a Finder window.
62	
63	Below these two, **Duplicate as New Graphic…** makes a copy of the module for the selected clips. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
64	
65	## Diagnostics
66	
67	Under the buttons, Source lists what the module says about the clip, under a heading for each stage:
68	
69	- **Compiling the module** appears when there's something to report: the compile error, or the warnings the module's top level gave.
70	- **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** means that frame drew cleanly. **Checked at the clip's first frame** is followed by what that frame reported. Neither appears when the module didn't compile.
71	
72	The first frame is drawn at the clip's own size, so a missing font, a picture that isn't in the project or a size mismatch shows here. With several clips of one module selected, the check is of the first of them.
73	
74	Each row reads `line L, column C — message`, or the message alone when it has no place in the file. An error is in the stronger text colour and a warning is muted.
75	
76	While you drag a control, the list holds still. It updates when you let go.
77	
78	### Open a diagnostic
79	
80	Click a diagnostic, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor. This opens the file, not the line, so note the line number first.
81	
82	### In the graphics folder
83	
84	**In the graphics folder** lists what Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch when it scanned the project's graphics folder:
85	
86	- A module or picture with a bad name.
87	- An empty file.
88	- A font that loads no face.
89	- A file that couldn't be watched.
90	
91	Each row has a **Reveal** button, and clicking it or the row shows the graphics folder in Finder, not the file. These rows count as warnings in the section's summary.
92	
93	## A missing module
94	
95	When the module's file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are disabled, **Revision** reads `missing`, and Source shows the error `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`.
96	
97	If Frame Job kept an earlier version, you can [restore it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
98	
99	## Several modules selected
100	
101	When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, Source's summary counts them, such as `2 modules`. It names them and says:
102	
103	> Drawn by different modules: lower-third, title-card
104	>
105	> Select one module's clips to edit its properties.
106	
107	The rows, buttons and diagnostics are gone until you do. **Size** stays editable, because it doesn't depend on the module. **Properties** needs one module and **Timeline** needs one clip.
108	
109	## Switching clips to another module
110	
111	The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy.
112	
113	To move clips to an existing module, delete them and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again, or have an agent do it with `set_graphic`.
114	
115	## Related
116	
117	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
118	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
119	- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
120	- [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/)
121

1	---
2	title: Graphic properties
3	description: Change what a graphic shows with its property rows, put values back to the module's defaults, and clear values the module no longer uses.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	A module decides what can be changed about a graphic, such as a title, a colour or a size. Each of those is a property with its own row in the **Properties** section, so you can change what a graphic shows without touching its code.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  keys={['↩', '⇧↩']}
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties"
14	  tools="set_graphic"
15	/>
16	
17	<Shot
18	  name="07-clip-graphic.inspector"
19	  alt="The Properties section of a lower third, open under the Graphic sub-tab. Title and subtitle are text fields reading Jane Doe and Director of Photography. accent is an orange colour swatch. size has a slider beside a field reading 64. boxed is a ticked checkbox. align is a pop-up reading left."
20	/>
21	
22	## Property rows
23	
24	Properties shows one row for each property the module declares, in the module's own order. A row's label is the one the module gives it, or the property's key when it gives none, and resting the pointer on the row shows the module's help text. The section starts open, and its summary counts the rows, such as `6 properties`.
25	
26	Every row is a normal inspector row. A change is one undo step, and you can right-click a row's label to reset it. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
27	
28	If there are no rows, the section says why:
29	
30	| It says | What it means |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| "The module declares no properties." | The graphic has nothing to set. |
33	| "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." | Frame Job can't read the module's properties until it's fixed. See [Diagnostics](/graphics/graphic-tab/#diagnostics). The clip's values are kept and listed as [stale values](#stale-values). |
34	
35	A module gives each property one of six types, and the type sets the control.
36	
37	### Number
38	
39	A value field, with a slider beside it when the module gives both a minimum and a maximum. A number past the range is held to the end of the range.
40	
41	The field shows two decimals when the module's step is below 1. With no step, it shows two decimals when the default or a bound has a fraction. Otherwise it shows whole numbers.
42	
43	### String
44	
45	A one-line field the width of the inspector. Long text scrolls inside it.
46	
47	When the module marks the property as multi-line, it's a text area instead: <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line.
48	
49	A property holds at most 4,096 characters.
50	
51	### Boolean
52	
53	A checkbox.
54	
55	### Enum
56	
57	A pop-up of the module's options, of which there can be 1 to 32.
58	
59	### Color
60	
61	A colour swatch. Click it to open the macOS colour panel. A colour you can see through keeps its opacity.
62	
63	### Asset
64	
65	A pop-up of pictures. It lists **None**, then every picture in the project's graphics, then any picture name that's referred to but missing from the folder. A missing name comes from the selected clips, the selected action's end or the module's default, so a missing picture still shows by name.
66	
67	**None** draws no picture, even when the module has a default one.
68	
69	To add a picture to the list, choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…** first. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
70	
71	## Reset
72	
73	A **Reset** button appears on the section's header while a row differs from the module's default. Click it to clear every value stored on the selected clips, so the module draws its own defaults. It's one undo step, named **Reset Graphic Properties**.
74	
75	To put back one row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
76	
77	While an action is selected, the rows edit the action's end, not the clip. The header shows **Clear** in the place of **Reset**, and right-clicking a row offers **Set end value to default**. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
78	
79	## Values at the default
80	
81	With no action selected, setting a value back to the module's default clears it from the clip. The clip then follows the module's default if that changes later.
82	
83	A colour counts as the default when its channels match, however the module spelled it.
84	
85	The exception is a property an action on the clip animates. There, Frame Job keeps the default as a stored value, so the animation keeps its start.
86	
87	## Editing several clips
88	
89	With several clips of one module selected, a change to a row applies to all of them, as one undo step. A row whose clips disagree shows the first clip's value with a **mixed** badge. See [Edit several clips at once](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
90	
91	Properties appears only when all the selected clips share one module. Clips of different modules can't be edited together, and an agent can't set their properties in one go either. See [Several modules selected](/graphics/graphic-tab/#several-modules-selected).
92	
93	## Stale values
94	
95	A clip can hold a value for a property the module no longer declares, for example after you rename a property in the module. The value stays, listed below the rows with its key dimmed, its value beside it, and **⌫** to remove it.
96	
97	The clip still draws. The value is passed to the module, and Source shows the warning `props.<key> is not in the schema; it is passed through`.
98	
99	**⌫** removes the value from every selected clip, as one undo step named **Remove Graphic Property**.
100	
101	With no compiled module, every stored value is listed this way. An action's end has stale rows of its own, marked as the action's. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
102	
103	## Good to know
104	
105	A stored value that no longer suits its property, such as a choice the module has dropped from an [Enum](#enum), isn't listed as stale. The clip draws the module's default, and Source shows a warning naming the property.
106	
107	## Related
108	
109	- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
110	- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
111	- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)
112	- [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/)

1	---
2	title: Share a graphic
3	description: Save a graphic as a .fjgraphic file with the fonts and pictures it uses, and bring one into another project.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A `.fjgraphic` file carries one graphic, with the fonts and pictures it uses, so you can move it to another project or give it to someone else with Frame Job. Finder calls the file a Frame Job Graphic.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
13	  where={['Export… and From File… in the Insert Graphic sheet', 'A .fjgraphic opened from the Finder']}
14	  tools={['export_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Export a graphic
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…** and pick the graphic in the Insert Graphic sheet. It can be a bundled template or one from **This Project**.
22	
23	2. Choose **Export…**. It's dimmed when the chosen graphic doesn't compile, and while another export is running.
24	
25	3. In the save panel, which slides down over the sheet with `<module>.fjgraphic` as the name, choose where to put the file and save.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	The Insert Graphic sheet stays open. The line under its lists says `Exporting <title>…`, then `Exported <title> to <file>:` followed by the files the package holds, or says why it couldn't.
30	
31	Saving over an existing file replaces it whole. If the export fails, the file already there is left as it was.
32	
33	Exporting changes nothing in the project and isn't an undo step.
34	
35	## What a package packs
36	
37	A package holds the module and only the project fonts and pictures the graphic uses. To find those, Frame Job draws the graphic and packs what it saw used:
38	
39	- Every frame with the default properties. A graphic longer than 900 frames has 900 frames spread evenly over it.
40	- Then each choice of each [Enum](/graphics/properties/#enum) property and the other value of each [Boolean](/graphics/properties/#boolean) property, one at a time, over 30 frames each. It draws at most 32 of these.
41	
42	A font is packed when the graphic drew or measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font lacks. A picture is packed when the graphic's `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are never packed, because every copy of Frame Job has them, so a bundled template's package holds its module and nothing else.
43	
44	A frame that fails to draw is skipped.
45	
46	:::caution
47	[String](/graphics/properties/#string) and [Asset](/graphics/properties/#asset) properties are only tried at their defaults. A font or picture the graphic reaches only through another value, such as a different title or another picture, isn't packed. Read the file list in the message line after an export, and if something's missing, make it that property's default in the module and export again.
48	:::
49	
50	## The .fjgraphic file
51	
52	A package is a zip with nothing compressed. It holds `manifest.json`, the module, and the `fonts/` and `assets/` folders. The manifest gives the package's format, the module, its title, category and description, the Frame Job version that wrote it, and each file's path, name, size and SHA-256.
53	
54	Exporting the same graphic twice with the same version of Frame Job gives byte-identical files.
55	
56	A file name a zip path can't hold is stored under a tidied name. That covers a `:` or `\`, a control character and a leading `.`, so `a:b.ttf` is stored as `a-b.ttf`. The manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and `asset(name)` still finds its picture.
57	
58	A package can hold at most about 4 GiB and 65,535 files.
59	
60	## Open from the Finder
61	
62	Double-click a `.fjgraphic`, open it with **Open With**, drop it on Frame Job's Dock icon, or open it from a browser's downloads. Frame Job [checks the package](#package-checks), then puts up the [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet).
63	
64	The package goes into the front project, the one whose window is in front. With no project open, it goes into a new untitled project. A package that fails its checks before the sheet appears shows an alert and opens no project.
65	
66	If Frame Job wasn't running, it opens first and the package waits until any projects it reopens are back, so it lands once, in one project, with no Welcome window.
67	
68	**File ▸ Open** doesn't list `.fjgraphic` files, and there's no menu item for importing one.
69	
70	## Import with From File…
71	
72	<Steps>
73	
74	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**. The Insert Graphic sheet closes and a file panel opens.
75	
76	2. Choose a `.fjgraphic`. The [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet) appears for that same project.
77	
78	</Steps>
79	
80	The panel also takes a `.js` module, which goes straight onto the timeline. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
81	
82	## The Import Graphic sheet
83	
84	Before anything is copied, the sheet shows the graphic's title and description, then what will happen to each file:
85	
86	| Line | What it can read |
87	| --- | --- |
88	| Module | `Module: lower-third`, `Module: lower-third (already in this project)`, or `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)` |
89	| Fonts | The font files, each plain, marked `(already here)`, or marked `(as Inter-2.ttf)`. With none, `Fonts: none`. |
90	| Pictures | The picture files, each plain or marked `(already here)`. With none, `Pictures: none`. |
91	
92	Under them it says "Importing copies these files into this project's graphics. It is not an Undo step."
93	
94	Choose **Import** to copy the files, or **Cancel** to copy nothing.
95	
96	If the project's graphics folder changed while the sheet was up and the import can't go ahead, Frame Job beeps, the sheet stays open and it says why.
97	
98	## Name clashes
99	
100	An import never replaces a file. Each file keeps the name the package gives it, unless that name is taken:
101	
102	| The project already has | What happens |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| A file of that name with the same contents | It's used as it is, and the sheet says "already here". |
105	| A different module of that name | The module is copied under a new name with `-2`, `-3` and so on: `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)`. |
106	| A different font of that name | The font is copied under a new name, such as `as Inter-2.ttf`. A font is found by its family, so its file name changes nothing. |
107	| A different picture of that name | The import stops, because the module asks for its pictures by name. An alert says so. Rename or remove the project's file and import again. |
108	
109	A name that differs only in case counts as taken. A module name also counts as taken while clips left behind by a [deleted graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/) still use it.
110	
111	To find the project's pictures, see [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
112	
113	## After an import
114	
115	**Import** copies the files into the project's graphics folder and opens the Insert Graphic sheet on **This Project** with the graphic chosen, ready to insert. The line under the lists says what happened:
116	
117	`Imported Lower third as lower-third. Added: lower-third.js, fonts/Inter.ttf. Already here: assets/logo.png.`
118	
119	An import only copies files. It places no clip, so choose **Insert** when you want one on the timeline.
120	
121	Importing isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. An untitled project keeps the files when it's first saved. If a copy fails part-way, what it had copied is removed.
122	
123	## Package checks
124	
125	Frame Job checks a package before it copies anything, and a check that fails writes nothing. The message reads `<file> cannot be imported:` followed by the reason.
126	
127	| What's wrong | What the reason says |
128	| --- | --- |
129	| The file is empty | `it is empty (0 bytes)` |
130	| It isn't a zip, or it's damaged | For example `the package is not a zip: no end of central directory record` |
131	| It was compressed, for example by zipping it again | `<entry> is compressed (method 8); a .fjgraphic holds stored entries only` |
132	| It was changed after it was written | The entry that differs from the manifest by path, size or SHA-256, such as `<entry> is 2048 bytes, but the manifest says 1024` |
133	| A newer Frame Job wrote it | `the package is format 2; this Frame Job reads format 1 — a newer Frame Job wrote it` |
134	| A font is bad | `the font "<name>" is not a .ttf or .otf file`, or why it doesn't load |
135	| A picture is bad | `the picture "<name>"` and why: it isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file, its name can't be used, or it's empty |
136	
137	A module that doesn't compile passes these checks and is imported. It's listed on **This Project** with **Export…** dimmed, and **Insert** places nothing and shows the first error. Fix it the way you'd fix any module. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
138	
139	## With an agent
140	
141	`export_graphic` is **Export…**, writing to a path instead of through a save panel, and it also says how many frames it drew and how many failed. The assistant asks you before it runs, because it can replace a file.
142	
143	`import_graphic` is **Import** without the sheet, so nothing asks first. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
144	
145	## Related
146	
147	- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
148	- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
149	- [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/)
150	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
151

1	---
2	title: The Graphic sub-tab
3	description: See which module draws a graphic clip, open it in your editor, and read what it reports when it doesn't draw as it should.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	Select a graphic clip and the inspector's **Clip** tab gains a **Graphic** sub-tab. It's where you set what the graphic shows, see which module draws it, and find out what's wrong when it doesn't draw as it should.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic" tools={['set_graphic', 'get_graphic']} />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="07-clip-graphic.inspector"
15	  alt="The Clip tab with a graphic clip selected. Graphic, Picture and Clip sub-tabs sit above four sections. Source is collapsed and reads Lower third. Properties is open with six rows: Title, subtitle, accent, size, boxed and align. Size is collapsed and reads 960 × 540, and Timeline is collapsed and reads 00:00:05:00."
16	/>
17	
18	## The Graphic sub-tab
19	
20	A graphic clip's sub-tabs are **Graphic**, **Picture** and **Clip**, in that order. **Graphic** appears only when every selected clip is a graphic clip, so any other kind of clip in the selection removes it.
21	
22	| Section | What it's for | Summary when collapsed | Starts | Shows |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| [Source](#source) | What draws the clip, and what the module reports about it | The error or warning count, or the module's name | Collapsed | Always |
25	| [Properties](/graphics/properties/) | What the graphic shows | The number of properties | Open | When every selected clip is drawn by one module |
26	| [Size](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's width and height | `W × H` | Collapsed | Always |
27	| [Timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's own timeline | Its length | Collapsed | With one clip selected |
28	
29	There's no **Color** sub-tab. To grade a graphic, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above it.
30	
31	## The Picture sub-tab
32	
33	A graphic has the same layer settings as other clips, so you can move, scale and fade it: [Transform](/canvas/transform/) (position, scale, rotation and opacity), [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/), [Shadow](/effects/shadow/), [Filters](/effects/filters/), [Reflection](/effects/reflection/), [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) and [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
34	
35	It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, which are for clips drawn from media.
36	
37	## The Clip sub-tab
38	
39	**Clip** has the clip's [Timing](/editing/timing-section/) when one clip is selected, [Transition](/motion/transition-settings/) when the clip overlaps the one before it, and [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
40	
41	There's no Speed section. A graphic has no speed control or speed ramp, because its timing comes from the module and its [Length](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
42	
43	## Source
44	
45	Source says what draws the clip. Its summary, when collapsed, is `1 error` or `2 warnings` if there's anything to report, and otherwise the module's name.
46	
47	### Name, File and Revision
48	
49	| Row | What it shows |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **Name** | The module's display name, or its file name when it has none |
52	| **File** | The module's file, `<name>.js` |
53	| **Revision** | The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the file's text, which change whenever the text does, or `missing` when the file is gone |
54	
55	### Open in Editor
56	
57	**Open in Editor** opens the module in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files. Save there and the preview redraws within a moment. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
58	
59	### Reveal in Finder
60	
61	**Reveal in Finder** shows the module's file in a Finder window.
62	
63	Below these two, **Duplicate as New Graphic…** makes a copy of the module for the selected clips. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
64	
65	## Diagnostics
66	
67	Under the buttons, Source lists what the module says about the clip, under a heading for each stage:
68	
69	- **Compiling the module** appears when there's something to report: the compile error, or the warnings the module's top level gave.
70	- **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** means that frame drew cleanly. **Checked at the clip's first frame** is followed by what that frame reported. Neither appears when the module didn't compile.
71	
72	The first frame is drawn at the clip's own size, so a missing font, a picture that isn't in the project or a size mismatch shows here. With several clips of one module selected, the check is of the first of them.
73	
74	Each row reads `line L, column C — message`, or the message alone when it has no place in the file. An error is in the stronger text colour and a warning is muted.
75	
76	While you drag a control, the list holds still. It updates when you let go.
77	
78	### Open a diagnostic
79	
80	Click a diagnostic, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor. This opens the file, not the line, so note the line number first.
81	
82	### In the graphics folder
83	
84	**In the graphics folder** lists what Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch when it scanned the project's graphics folder:
85	
86	- A module or picture with a bad name.
87	- An empty file.
88	- A font that loads no face.
89	- A file that couldn't be watched.
90	
91	Each row has a **Reveal** button, and clicking it or the row shows the graphics folder in Finder, not the file. These rows count as warnings in the section's summary.
92	
93	## A missing module
94	
95	When the module's file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are disabled, **Revision** reads `missing`, and Source shows the error `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`.
96	
97	If Frame Job kept an earlier version, you can [restore it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
98	
99	## Several modules selected
100	
101	When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, Source's summary counts them, such as `2 modules`. It names them and says:
102	
103	> Drawn by different modules: lower-third, title-card
104	>
105	> Select one module's clips to edit its properties.
106	
107	The rows, buttons and diagnostics are gone until you do. **Size** stays editable, because it doesn't depend on the module. **Properties** needs one module and **Timeline** needs one clip.
108	
109	## Switching clips to another module
110	
111	The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy.
112	
113	To move clips to an existing module, delete them and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again, or have an agent do it with `set_graphic`.
114

22	## Property rows
23	
24	Properties shows one row for each property the module declares, in the module's own order. A row's label is the one the module gives it, or the property's key when it gives none, and resting the pointer on the row shows the module's help text. The section starts open, and its summary counts the rows, such as `6 properties`.
25	
26	Every row is a normal inspector row. A change is one undo step, and you can right-click a row's label to reset it. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
27	
28	If there are no rows, the section says why:
29	
30	| It says | What it means |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| "The module declares no properties." | The graphic has nothing to set. |
33	| "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." | Frame Job can't read the module's properties until it's fixed. See [Diagnostics](/graphics/graphic-tab/#diagnostics). The clip's values are kept and listed as [stale values](#stale-values). |
34	
35	A module gives each property one of six types, and the type sets the control.
36	
37	### Number
38	
39	A value field, with a slider beside it when the module gives both a minimum and a maximum. A number past the range is held to the end of the range.
40	
41	The field shows two decimals when the module's step is below 1. With no step, it shows two decimals when the default or a bound has a fraction. Otherwise it shows whole numbers.
42	
43	### String
44	
45	A one-line field the width of the inspector. Long text scrolls inside it.
46	
47	When the module marks the property as multi-line, it's a text area instead: <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line.
48	
49	A property holds at most 4,096 characters.
50	
51	### Boolean
52	
53	A checkbox.
54	
55	### Enum
56	
57	A pop-up of the module's options, of which there can be 1 to 32.
58	
59	### Color
60	
61	A colour swatch. Click it to open the macOS colour panel. A colour you can see through keeps its opacity.
62	
63	### Asset
64	
65	A pop-up of pictures. It lists **None**, then every picture in the project's graphics, then any picture name that's referred to but missing from the folder. A missing name comes from the selected clips, the selected action's end or the module's default, so a missing picture still shows by name.
66	
67	**None** draws no picture, even when the module has a default one.
68	
69	To add a picture to the list, choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…** first. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
70	
71	## Reset
72	
73	A **Reset** button appears on the section's header while a row differs from the module's default. Click it to clear every value stored on the selected clips, so the module draws its own defaults. It's one undo step, named **Reset Graphic Properties**.
74	
75	To put back one row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
76	
77	While an action is selected, the rows edit the action's end, not the clip. The header shows **Clear** in the place of **Reset**, and right-clicking a row offers **Set end value to default**. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
78	
79	## Values at the default
80	
81	With no action selected, setting a value back to the module's default clears it from the clip. The clip then follows the module's default if that changes later.
82	
83	A colour counts as the default when its channels match, however the module spelled it.
84	
85	The exception is a property an action on the clip animates. There, Frame Job keeps the default as a stored value, so the animation keeps its start.
86	
87	## Editing several clips
88	
89	With several clips of one module selected, a change to a row applies to all of them, as one undo step. A row whose clips disagree shows the first clip's value with a **mixed** badge. See [Edit several clips at once](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
90	
91	Properties appears only when all the selected clips share one module. Clips of different modules can't be edited together, and an agent can't set their properties in one go either. See [Several modules selected](/graphics/graphic-tab/#several-modules-selected).
92	
93	## Stale values
94	
95	A clip can hold a value for a property the module no longer declares, for example after you rename a property in the module. The value stays, listed below the rows with its key dimmed, its value beside it, and **⌫** to remove it.
96	
97	The clip still draws. The value is passed to the module, and Source shows the warning `props.<key> is not in the schema; it is passed through`.
98	
99	**⌫** removes the value from every selected clip, as one undo step named **Remove Graphic Property**.
100	
101	With no compiled module, every stored value is listed this way. An action's end has stale rows of its own, marked as the action's. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
102	
103	## Good to know
104	
105	A stored value that no longer suits its property, such as a choice the module has dropped from an [Enum](#enum), isn't listed as stale. The clip draws the module's default, and Source shows a warning naming the property.
106

1	// app/Sources/GraphicPackage.swift — the Graphic dialog's Export… and
2	// `export_graphic` (spec §11 G-46): one graphic written as a `.fjgraphic`
3	// package holding its module and only the project fonts and assets the
4	// engine saw it use.
5	//
6	// **A job is built on main and written off it.** `GraphicPackageJob.project`
7	// and `.template` read the document on main: the module's bytes, its title,
8	// category and description (`GraphicCatalog`), its size and length
9	// (`AgentServer.metaWhole`, as `render_graphic` reads them), and a FRESH
10	// library (`GraphicStore.makeIndexedLibrary()`; a template's holds the
11	// bundled faces alone). `write(to:)` runs QuickJS, so it runs only on the
12	// sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server thread — never main, never GCD.
13	//
14	// **The usage rule** (G-46 (b)): the module is compiled against that library
15	// and drawn — every frame up to `maxFrames` with its default props, else
16	// `maxFrames` evenly spaced, each `svg` then `rasterize` — and then each
17	// variant (an `enum` option other than the default, a boolean's opposite, in
18	// schema order, at most `maxVariants`) over `variantFrames` evenly spaced
19	// frames, every other prop at its default. The library's `usage()` is then
20	// every project font blob and asset to pack; a bundled face never is. A
21	// frame that throws is skipped and counted.
22	//
23	// **The file** is the core's (`ReelGraphicPackage.write`): written as
24	// `.<file>.partial` beside the destination and renamed over it, so an
25	// existing file is replaced whole; any throw removes the partial file.
26	
27	import Foundation
28	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
29	
30	enum GraphicPackage {
31	    static let fileExtension = "fjgraphic", typeIdentifier = "com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic"
32	    static let maxFrames = 900, variantFrames = 30, maxVariants = 32
33	
34	    /// The exported type (`project.yml`), else data by its extension (spec §11 G-47 (g)).
35	    static var contentType: UTType {
36	        UTType(typeIdentifier)
37	            ?? UTType(filenameExtension: fileExtension, conformingTo: .data) ?? .data
38	    }
39	
40	    /// The manifest's `app_version`: the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`, else "".
41	    static var appVersion: String {
42	        Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? ""
43	    }
44	
45	    /// Every frame of `length` when there are at most `cap`, else `cap` frames evenly spaced
46	    /// from the first to the last.
47	    static func sampledFrames(length: Int, cap: Int) -> [Int] {
48	        guard length > cap else { return Array(0..<max(length, 0)) }
49	        guard cap > 1 else { return cap == 1 ? [0] : [] }
50	        return (0..<cap).map { i in
51	            Int((Double(i) * Double(length - 1) / Double(cap - 1)).rounded())
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    /// The props of each variant G-46 (b) draws: one per `enum` option other than its
56	    /// default and one per boolean's opposite, in schema order, at most `maxVariants`.
57	    static func variants(_ schema: GraphicSchema) -> [[String: Any]] {
58	        var out: [[String: Any]] = []
59	        for entry in schema.entries {
60	            switch (entry.type, entry.default) {
61	            case ("enum", let value):
62	                let current: String? = { if case .string(let s) = value { return s }; return nil }()
63	                for option in entry.options where option != current {
64	                    out.append([entry.key: option])
65	                }
66	            case ("boolean", .bool(let flag)):
67	                out.append([entry.key: !flag])
68	            default:
69	                continue
70	            }
71	        }
72	        return Array(out.prefix(maxVariants))
73	    }
74	}

77	struct GraphicPackageResult {
78	    let url: URL
79	    /// The manifest's in-package paths, in order; `manifest.json` itself is not among them.
80	    let files: [String]
81	    /// Every frame drawn (the defaults' and the variants'), and how many of them threw.
82	    let frames: Int
83	    let failedFrames: Int
84	}

86	/// One graphic, read off the document on main, ready to be written off it.
87	struct GraphicPackageJob {
88	    let name: String
89	    /// What a compile failure names: `graphics/<name>.js` or `the template "<name>"`.
90	    let label: String
91	    let title: String
92	    let category: String
93	    let description: String?
94	    let source: Data
95	    let library: GraphicLibrary
96	    /// The library's font blobs: the project file each came from, nil for a bundled face.
97	    let fonts: [GraphicFile?]
98	    let assets: [GraphicFile]
99	    let width: Int
100	    let height: Int
101	    let length: Int
102	    let fps: Fps
103	    let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
104	    let appVersion: String
105	
106	    /// A This Project module, read on main. Throws the store's sentence when the folder does
107	    /// not hold it.
108	    static func project(named name: String, document: ProjectDocument) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
109	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else {
110	            throw ReelCoreError(message: ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
111	        }
112	        let indexed = try store.makeIndexedLibrary()
113	        guard let file = indexed.scan.modules[name] else {
114	            throw ReelCoreError(message: store.noModuleSentence(name))
115	        }
116	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
117	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _)? = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(
118	            named: name, for: document.recipeKey)
119	        {
120	            meta = described
121	        }
122	        return try make(
123	            name: name, label: "graphics/\(name).js", meta: meta, source: file.bytes,
124	            library: indexed.library, fonts: indexed.fonts, assets: indexed.scan.assets,
125	            document: document)
126	    }
127	
128	    /// A bundled template, read on main, with a library of the bundled faces alone.
129	    static func template(
130	        _ entry: GraphicTemplateLibrary.Entry, document: ProjectDocument
131	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
132	        let name = entry.template.name
133	        let source: Data
134	        do {
135	            source = try Data(contentsOf: entry.template.url)
136	        } catch {
137	            throw ReelCoreError(
138	                message: "\(entry.template.url.path) could not be read: "
139	                    + error.localizedDescription)
140	        }
141	        let library = GraphicLibrary()
142	        var fonts: [GraphicFile?] = []
143	        for url in GraphicStore.bundledFontURLs(in: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory) {
144	            try library.addFont(Data(contentsOf: url))
145	            fonts.append(nil)
146	        }
147	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
148	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _) = entry.entry { meta = described }
149	        return try make(
150	            name: name, label: "the template \"\(name)\"", meta: meta, source: source,
151	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: [], document: document)
152	    }
153	
154	    private static func make(
155	        name: String, label: String, meta: [String: Any], source: Data, library: GraphicLibrary,
156	        fonts: [GraphicFile?], assets: [GraphicFile], document: ProjectDocument
157	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
158	        let canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
159	        let tick = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
160	        let width: Int, height: Int, length: Int
161	        do {
162	            width = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "width", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
163	                ?? canvas.width
164	            height = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "height", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
165	                ?? canvas.height
166	            length = try AgentServer.metaWhole(
167	                meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(tick))
168	                ?? Int((5 * canvas.fps.double).rounded(.up))
169	        } catch let error as AgentServer.ToolError {
170	            throw ReelCoreError(message: error.message)
171	        }
172	        return GraphicPackageJob(
173	            name: name, label: label, title: GraphicCatalog.title(meta: meta, name: name),
174	            category: GraphicCatalog.category(meta: meta),
175	            description: GraphicCatalog.description(meta: meta), source: source,
176	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: assets, width: width, height: height,
177	            length: length, fps: canvas.fps, canvas: canvas, appVersion: GraphicPackage.appVersion)
178	    }
179	
180	    /// Compiles, draws by G-46 (b)'s rule, and writes the package at `url`, replacing a file
181	    /// there. Never on main and never on GCD: the sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server
182	    /// thread. Throws a sentence, writing nothing, for a module that does not compile.
183	    func write(to url: URL) throws -> GraphicPackageResult {
184	        let module: GraphicModule
185	        do {
186	            module = try GraphicModule.compile(
187	                library: library, name: name, source: String(decoding: source, as: UTF8.self),
188	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
189	        } catch {
190	            let first = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error).first
191	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
192	            throw ReelCoreError(
193	                message: "\(label) does not compile: " + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic")
194	                    + line)
195	        }
196	        let describe = module.describeJSON()
197	        let described = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(describe.utf8)))
198	            as? [String: Any]
199	        let schema = GraphicSchema(
200	            describeJSON: describe, schema: described?["schema"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:])
201	        var frames = 0, failed = 0
202	        let sample = { (frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) in
203	            frames += 1
204	            if !self.draw(module, frame: frame, props: props) { failed += 1 }
205	        }
206	        for frame in GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.maxFrames) {
207	            sample(frame, [:])
208	        }
209	        let variantFrames = GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(
210	            length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.variantFrames)
211	        for props in GraphicPackage.variants(schema) {
212	            for frame in variantFrames { sample(frame, props) }
213	        }
214	
215	        let usage = library.usage()
216	        let usedFonts = usage.fonts.compactMap { fonts.indices.contains($0) ? fonts[$0] : nil }
217	        let usedAssets = usage.assets.compactMap { used in assets.first { $0.name == used } }
218	        var listed: [[String: Any]] = [["path": "\(name).js", "size": source.count]]
219	        var data = source
220	        for (folder, files) in [
221	            (GraphicStore.fontsFolderName, usedFonts), (GraphicStore.assetsFolderName, usedAssets),
222	        ] {
223	            for file in files {
224	                listed.append(["path": "\(folder)/\(file.name)", "size": file.bytes.count])
225	                data.append(file.bytes)
226	            }
227	        }
228	        let spec: [String: Any] = [
229	            "module": name, "title": title, "category": category,
230	            "description": description ?? NSNull(), "app_version": appVersion, "files": listed,
231	        ]
232	        let specJSON = String(
233	            decoding: try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: spec), as: UTF8.self)
234	
235	        let partial = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
236	            .appendingPathComponent(".\(url.lastPathComponent).partial")
237	        let manifest: String
238	        do {
239	            manifest = try ReelGraphicPackage.write(
240	                path: partial.path, packageJSON: specJSON, data: data)
241	            guard rename(partial.path, url.path) == 0 else {
242	                let why = String(cString: strerror(errno))
243	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(url.path) could not be replaced: \(why)")
244	            }
245	        } catch {
246	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: partial)
247	            throw error
248	        }
249	        let parsed = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(manifest.utf8)))
250	            as? [String: Any]
251	        let paths = (parsed?["files"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? [])
252	            .compactMap { $0["path"] as? String }
253	        return GraphicPackageResult(url: url, files: paths, frames: frames, failedFrames: failed)
254	    }
255	
256	    /// One frame drawn and rasterized at the graphic's size; false when either threw.
257	    private func draw(_ module: GraphicModule, frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) -> Bool {
258	        let ctx = AgentServer.graphicContext(
259	            frame: frame, fps: fps, length: length, width: width, height: height, canvas: canvas)
260	        guard let ctxData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ctx),
261	            let propsData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: props)
262	        else { return false }
263	        do {
264	            let drawn = try module.svg(
265	                frame: frame, propsJSON: String(decoding: propsData, as: UTF8.self),
266	                ctxJSON: String(decoding: ctxData, as: UTF8.self),
267	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
268	            _ = try library.rasterize(drawn.svg, width: width, height: height)
269	            return true
270	        } catch {
271	            return false
272	        }
273	    }
274	}

418	        let job: GraphicPackageJob
419	        do {

423	                    throw ReelCoreError(

427	            case .project:

429	            }

432	            messageLabel.stringValue = Self.sentence(error)

436	        exportButton.isEnabled = false

439	            let outcome = Result { try job.write(to: url) }
440	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in self?.exportFinished(job, outcome) }
441	        }
442	        thread.stackSize = GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes
443	        thread.name = "com.kgalligan.framejob.graphic-export"

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points

  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,

  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).

  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;

  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).

  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. The rows (`OP_TABLE`) and `OP_NAMES` live in
  `op_rows.rs` (road map "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T1, a pure move),
  re-exported by `op_table.rs` so every `op_table::` path holds; an op's row
  is added there, and the four builders `req`, `opt`, `within` and `op` are
  `pub(crate)` for it. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-nine op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (thirty kinds — `reframe_clip` added `Follow` (its members end `layout`,
  `speaker`, `center`, `fit`, `keep`),
  `WhereEmpty` and `Subjects`, the last a caller-authored object declared
  and closed at every level; `switch_layout` added `Layout`,
  `LayoutShape`, `Corner` and `Point`, `[f64; 2]`; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.

  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified; `set_media_cursor`
  is refused inside like `set_media_speech` (twelve ops in all, `edit.rs`'s

  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

- `edit_speed_profile.rs` — what a rate edit scales (SR-19 (a), (b)), a pure

  - `scaled_profile`: scales the base, every end rate and every speed span.

- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized
