- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).

  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,

  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and

  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11

  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11

  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s

- `model_cursor.rs` · `cursor_props.rs` · `recipe_cursor.rs` — the cursor in the model and the

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

1	// app/Sources/GraphicPackage.swift — the Graphic dialog's Export… and
2	// `export_graphic` (spec §11 G-46): one graphic written as a `.fjgraphic`
3	// package holding its module and only the project fonts and assets the
4	// engine saw it use.
5	//
6	// **A job is built on main and written off it.** `GraphicPackageJob.project`
7	// and `.template` read the document on main: the module's bytes, its title,
8	// category and description (`GraphicCatalog`), its size and length
9	// (`AgentServer.metaWhole`, as `render_graphic` reads them), and a FRESH
10	// library (`GraphicStore.makeIndexedLibrary()`; a template's holds the
11	// bundled faces alone). `write(to:)` runs QuickJS, so it runs only on the
12	// sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server thread — never main, never GCD.
13	//
14	// **The usage rule** (G-46 (b)): the module is compiled against that library
15	// and drawn — every frame up to `maxFrames` with its default props, else
16	// `maxFrames` evenly spaced, each `svg` then `rasterize` — and then each
17	// variant (an `enum` option other than the default, a boolean's opposite, in
18	// schema order, at most `maxVariants`) over `variantFrames` evenly spaced
19	// frames, every other prop at its default. The library's `usage()` is then
20	// every project font blob and asset to pack; a bundled face never is. A
21	// frame that throws is skipped and counted.
22	//
23	// **The file** is the core's (`ReelGraphicPackage.write`): written as
24	// `.<file>.partial` beside the destination and renamed over it, so an
25	// existing file is replaced whole; any throw removes the partial file.
26	
27	import Foundation
28	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
29	
30	enum GraphicPackage {
31	    static let fileExtension = "fjgraphic", typeIdentifier = "com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic"
32	    static let maxFrames = 900, variantFrames = 30, maxVariants = 32
33	
34	    /// The exported type (`project.yml`), else data by its extension (spec §11 G-47 (g)).
35	    static var contentType: UTType {
36	        UTType(typeIdentifier)
37	            ?? UTType(filenameExtension: fileExtension, conformingTo: .data) ?? .data
38	    }
39	
40	    /// The manifest's `app_version`: the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`, else "".
41	    static var appVersion: String {
42	        Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? ""
43	    }
44	
45	    /// Every frame of `length` when there are at most `cap`, else `cap` frames evenly spaced
46	    /// from the first to the last.
47	    static func sampledFrames(length: Int, cap: Int) -> [Int] {
48	        guard length > cap else { return Array(0..<max(length, 0)) }
49	        guard cap > 1 else { return cap == 1 ? [0] : [] }
50	        return (0..<cap).map { i in
51	            Int((Double(i) * Double(length - 1) / Double(cap - 1)).rounded())
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    /// The props of each variant G-46 (b) draws: one per `enum` option other than its
56	    /// default and one per boolean's opposite, in schema order, at most `maxVariants`.
57	    static func variants(_ schema: GraphicSchema) -> [[String: Any]] {
58	        var out: [[String: Any]] = []
59	        for entry in schema.entries {
60	            switch (entry.type, entry.default) {
61	            case ("enum", let value):
62	                let current: String? = { if case .string(let s) = value { return s }; return nil }()
63	                for option in entry.options where option != current {
64	                    out.append([entry.key: option])
65	                }
66	            case ("boolean", .bool(let flag)):
67	                out.append([entry.key: !flag])
68	            default:
69	                continue
70	            }
71	        }
72	        return Array(out.prefix(maxVariants))
73	    }
74	}
75	
76	/// What one export wrote.
77	struct GraphicPackageResult {
78	    let url: URL
79	    /// The manifest's in-package paths, in order; `manifest.json` itself is not among them.
80	    let files: [String]
81	    /// Every frame drawn (the defaults' and the variants'), and how many of them threw.
82	    let frames: Int
83	    let failedFrames: Int
84	}
85	
86	/// One graphic, read off the document on main, ready to be written off it.
87	struct GraphicPackageJob {
88	    let name: String
89	    /// What a compile failure names: `graphics/<name>.js` or `the template "<name>"`.
90	    let label: String
91	    let title: String
92	    let category: String
93	    let description: String?
94	    let source: Data
95	    let library: GraphicLibrary
96	    /// The library's font blobs: the project file each came from, nil for a bundled face.
97	    let fonts: [GraphicFile?]
98	    let assets: [GraphicFile]
99	    let width: Int
100	    let height: Int
101	    let length: Int
102	    let fps: Fps
103	    let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
104	    let appVersion: String
105	
106	    /// A This Project module, read on main. Throws the store's sentence when the folder does
107	    /// not hold it.
108	    static func project(named name: String, document: ProjectDocument) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
109	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else {
110	            throw ReelCoreError(message: ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
111	        }
112	        let indexed = try store.makeIndexedLibrary()
113	        guard let file = indexed.scan.modules[name] else {
114	            throw ReelCoreError(message: store.noModuleSentence(name))
115	        }
116	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
117	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _)? = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(
118	            named: name, for: document.recipeKey)
119	        {
120	            meta = described
121	        }
122	        return try make(
123	            name: name, label: "graphics/\(name).js", meta: meta, source: file.bytes,
124	            library: indexed.library, fonts: indexed.fonts, assets: indexed.scan.assets,
125	            document: document)
126	    }
127	
128	    /// A bundled template, read on main, with a library of the bundled faces alone.
129	    static func template(
130	        _ entry: GraphicTemplateLibrary.Entry, document: ProjectDocument
131	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
132	        let name = entry.template.name
133	        let source: Data
134	        do {
135	            source = try Data(contentsOf: entry.template.url)
136	        } catch {
137	            throw ReelCoreError(
138	                message: "\(entry.template.url.path) could not be read: "
139	                    + error.localizedDescription)
140	        }
141	        let library = GraphicLibrary()
142	        var fonts: [GraphicFile?] = []
143	        for url in GraphicStore.bundledFontURLs(in: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory) {
144	            try library.addFont(Data(contentsOf: url))
145	            fonts.append(nil)
146	        }
147	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
148	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _) = entry.entry { meta = described }
149	        return try make(
150	            name: name, label: "the template \"\(name)\"", meta: meta, source: source,
151	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: [], document: document)
152	    }
153	
154	    private static func make(
155	        name: String, label: String, meta: [String: Any], source: Data, library: GraphicLibrary,
156	        fonts: [GraphicFile?], assets: [GraphicFile], document: ProjectDocument
157	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
158	        let canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
159	        let tick = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
160	        let width: Int, height: Int, length: Int
161	        do {
162	            width = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "width", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
163	                ?? canvas.width
164	            height = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "height", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
165	                ?? canvas.height
166	            length = try AgentServer.metaWhole(
167	                meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(tick))
168	                ?? Int((5 * canvas.fps.double).rounded(.up))
169	        } catch let error as AgentServer.ToolError {
170	            throw ReelCoreError(message: error.message)
171	        }
172	        return GraphicPackageJob(
173	            name: name, label: label, title: GraphicCatalog.title(meta: meta, name: name),
174	            category: GraphicCatalog.category(meta: meta),
175	            description: GraphicCatalog.description(meta: meta), source: source,
176	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: assets, width: width, height: height,
177	            length: length, fps: canvas.fps, canvas: canvas, appVersion: GraphicPackage.appVersion)
178	    }
179	
180	    /// Compiles, draws by G-46 (b)'s rule, and writes the package at `url`, replacing a file
181	    /// there. Never on main and never on GCD: the sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server
182	    /// thread. Throws a sentence, writing nothing, for a module that does not compile.
183	    func write(to url: URL) throws -> GraphicPackageResult {
184	        let module: GraphicModule
185	        do {
186	            module = try GraphicModule.compile(
187	                library: library, name: name, source: String(decoding: source, as: UTF8.self),
188	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
189	        } catch {
190	            let first = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error).first
191	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
192	            throw ReelCoreError(
193	                message: "\(label) does not compile: " + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic")
194	                    + line)
195	        }
196	        let describe = module.describeJSON()
197	        let described = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(describe.utf8)))
198	            as? [String: Any]
199	        let schema = GraphicSchema(
200	            describeJSON: describe, schema: described?["schema"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:])
201	        var frames = 0, failed = 0
202	        let sample = { (frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) in
203	            frames += 1
204	            if !self.draw(module, frame: frame, props: props) { failed += 1 }
205	        }
206	        for frame in GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.maxFrames) {
207	            sample(frame, [:])
208	        }
209	        let variantFrames = GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(
210	            length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.variantFrames)
211	        for props in GraphicPackage.variants(schema) {
212	            for frame in variantFrames { sample(frame, props) }
213	        }
214	
215	        let usage = library.usage()
216	        let usedFonts = usage.fonts.compactMap { fonts.indices.contains($0) ? fonts[$0] : nil }
217	        let usedAssets = usage.assets.compactMap { used in assets.first { $0.name == used } }
218	        var listed: [[String: Any]] = [["path": "\(name).js", "size": source.count]]
219	        var data = source
220	        for (folder, files) in [
221	            (GraphicStore.fontsFolderName, usedFonts), (GraphicStore.assetsFolderName, usedAssets),
222	        ] {
223	            for file in files {
224	                listed.append(["path": "\(folder)/\(file.name)", "size": file.bytes.count])
225	                data.append(file.bytes)
226	            }
227	        }
228	        let spec: [String: Any] = [
229	            "module": name, "title": title, "category": category,
230	            "description": description ?? NSNull(), "app_version": appVersion, "files": listed,
231	        ]
232	        let specJSON = String(
233	            decoding: try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: spec), as: UTF8.self)
234	
235	        let partial = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
236	            .appendingPathComponent(".\(url.lastPathComponent).partial")
237	        let manifest: String
238	        do {
239	            manifest = try ReelGraphicPackage.write(
240	                path: partial.path, packageJSON: specJSON, data: data)
241	            guard rename(partial.path, url.path) == 0 else {
242	                let why = String(cString: strerror(errno))
243	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(url.path) could not be replaced: \(why)")
244	            }
245	        } catch {
246	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: partial)
247	            throw error
248	        }
249	        let parsed = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(manifest.utf8)))
250	            as? [String: Any]
251	        let paths = (parsed?["files"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? [])
252	            .compactMap { $0["path"] as? String }
253	        return GraphicPackageResult(url: url, files: paths, frames: frames, failedFrames: failed)
254	    }
255	
256	    /// One frame drawn and rasterized at the graphic's size; false when either threw.
257	    private func draw(_ module: GraphicModule, frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) -> Bool {
258	        let ctx = AgentServer.graphicContext(
259	            frame: frame, fps: fps, length: length, width: width, height: height, canvas: canvas)
260	        guard let ctxData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ctx),
261	            let propsData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: props)
262	        else { return false }
263	        do {
264	            let drawn = try module.svg(
265	                frame: frame, propsJSON: String(decoding: propsData, as: UTF8.self),
266	                ctxJSON: String(decoding: ctxData, as: UTF8.self),
267	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
268	            _ = try library.rasterize(drawn.svg, width: width, height: height)
269	            return true
270	        } catch {
271	            return false
272	        }
273	    }
274	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift — Insert ▸ Graphic… (spec
2	// §11 G-45): a sheet of three panes — the categories, the graphics of the
3	// chosen one, and a looping preview of the chosen graphic with its title and
4	// one-line description — over a message line and a bottom bar of Export… and
5	// From File… at the left and Cancel and Insert at the right.
6	//
7	// **What it lists is `GraphicCatalog.categories(for:)`**, read once when the
8	// sheet is made, in the order `list_graphics` answers. It opens on the first
9	// category's first graphic; Insert is disabled with no graphic chosen, and a
10	// double-click on a graphic is Insert.
11	//
12	// **No second implementation.** Insert is one call of the editor's body —
13	// `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` with the template's URL, or
14	// `insertProjectGraphic(named:grouped:)` for This Project — the bodies the
15	// old menu items called, which call `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift`
16	// as `insert_graphic` does. It runs inside the button's event, so `grouped:
17	// false` (`applyEdit`). A success dismisses the sheet; a throw beeps and
18	// shows the sentence word for word in `messageLabel`, and the sheet stays.
19	//
20	// **What follows the sheet starts in `viewDidDisappear`**, for
21	// `ReverseProgressSheetController`'s reason: a sheet dismissed a moment ago
22	// is still the window's `attachedSheet`. From File… only sets a flag and
23	// dismisses; the open panel is begun there, once the browser is down. And
24	// the preview's render thread is stopped there, so every way out — Cancel,
25	// Esc, Insert, From File… — stops it.
26	//
27	// **Opened after an import** (spec §11 G-47 (f)) with `select`: This Project
28	// and the graphic of that name are chosen, and `message` is put in the
29	// message line after the choice has cleared it.
30	//
31	// **Export…** (spec §11 G-46 (a)) is enabled when the chosen graphic
32	// compiles and no export is running. It opens a save panel as a sheet on the
33	// browser, which stays up; `exportChosen(to:)` builds a `GraphicPackageJob` on
34	// main and writes it on a `Thread` of `GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes`
35	// (QuickJS needs the stack), and the result or the refusal goes in the
36	// message line. No edit and no undo step.
37	
38	import AppKit
39	
40	final class GraphicBrowserSheetController: NSViewController, NSTableViewDataSource,
41	    NSTableViewDelegate
42	{
43	    /// Weak, like every sheet's back-reference.
44	    private weak var document: ProjectDocument?
45	    private weak var editor: EditorViewController?
46	    private let categories: [GraphicBrowserCategory]
47	    private let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
48	    private var fromFilePending = false
49	    /// The graphic to choose and the message to show at load (G-47 (f)).
50	    private let select: String?
51	    private let message: String?
52	    /// An export's thread is running; Export… stays disabled until it reports.
53	    private(set) var exporting = false
54	    /// The last export's thread, for the probe to see it finish.
55	    private(set) var exportThread: Thread?
56	
57	    private let categoryTable = NSTableView()
58	    private let graphicTable = NSTableView()
59	    private let previewView = NSImageView()
60	    private let titleLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
61	    private let descriptionLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
62	    private let messageLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
63	    private let insertButton: NSButton
64	    private let fromFileButton: NSButton
65	    private let exportButton: NSButton
66	
67	    /// The preview's loop; its thread starts with the first graphic shown.
68	    private(set) lazy var player = GraphicPreviewPlayer(canvas: canvas) { [weak self] image in
69	        self?.showFrame(image)
70	    }
71	
72	    private static let width: CGFloat = 920
73	    private static let paneHeight: CGFloat = 410
74	    private static let categoriesWidth: CGFloat = 180
75	    private static let graphicsWidth: CGFloat = 240
76	    private static let gap: CGFloat = 12
77	    private static let cellID = NSUserInterfaceItemIdentifier("graphicbrowser.cell")
78	
79	    init(
80	        document: ProjectDocument, editor: EditorViewController, select: String? = nil,
81	        message: String? = nil
82	    ) {
83	        self.document = document
84	        self.editor = editor
85	        self.select = select
86	        self.message = message
87	        self.categories = GraphicCatalog.categories(for: document)
88	        self.canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
89	        self.insertButton = StickerButton(title: "Insert", style: .primary, target: nil, action: nil)
90	        self.fromFileButton = StickerButton(
91	            title: "From File…", style: .secondary, target: nil, action: nil)
92	        self.exportButton = StickerButton(
93	            title: "Export…", style: .secondary, target: nil, action: nil)
94	        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
95	    }
96	
97	    @available(*, unavailable)
98	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
99	        fatalError("GraphicBrowserSheetController does not support NSCoder")
100	    }
101	
102	    // MARK: - Layout
103	
104	    override func loadView() {
105	        let contentWidth = Self.width - sheetInset * 2
106	        let previewWidth = contentWidth - Self.categoriesWidth - Self.graphicsWidth - Self.gap * 2
107	        configure(categoryTable, id: "graphicbrowser.categories")
108	        categoryTable.allowsEmptySelection = false
109	        configure(graphicTable, id: "graphicbrowser.graphics")
110	        graphicTable.target = self
111	        graphicTable.doubleAction = #selector(graphicDoubleClicked(_:))
112	
113	        // The well at the canvas's aspect ratio, as large as the column allows
114	        // with the title and description under it.
115	        let room = NSSize(width: previewWidth, height: Self.paneHeight - 56)
116	        let aspect = CGFloat(max(canvas.width, 1)) / CGFloat(max(canvas.height, 1))
117	        let well = aspect >= room.width / room.height
118	            ? NSSize(width: room.width, height: (room.width / aspect).rounded())
119	            : NSSize(width: (room.height * aspect).rounded(), height: room.height)
120	        previewView.imageScaling = .scaleProportionallyUpOrDown
121	        previewView.wantsLayer = true
122	        previewView.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.canvasVoid.cgColor
123	        previewView.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.preview")
124	        previewView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
125	        previewView.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.width).isActive = true
126	        previewView.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.height).isActive = true
127	
128	        titleLabel.font = DS.sans(13, weight: .bold)
129	        titleLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
130	        titleLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
131	        titleLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.title")
132	        descriptionLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
133	        descriptionLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
134	        descriptionLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
135	        descriptionLabel.maximumNumberOfLines = 1
136	        descriptionLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.description")
137	        // A plain view with every edge pinned, so nothing in the column is
138	        // left to a stack's low-priority guesses.
139	        let previewColumn = NSView()
140	        previewColumn.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
141	        for label in [titleLabel, descriptionLabel] {
142	            label.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
143	            label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
144	        }
145	        for piece in [previewView, titleLabel, descriptionLabel] { previewColumn.addSubview(piece) }
146	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
147	            previewColumn.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
148	            previewColumn.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight),
149	            previewView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.topAnchor),
150	            previewView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
151	            titleLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewView.bottomAnchor, constant: 10),
152	            descriptionLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: titleLabel.bottomAnchor, constant: 6),
153	        ] + [titleLabel, descriptionLabel].flatMap { label in
154	            [
155	                label.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
156	                label.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
157	            ]
158	        })
159	
160	        let panes = NSStackView(views: [
161	            scroll(categoryTable, width: Self.categoriesWidth),
162	            scroll(graphicTable, width: Self.graphicsWidth), previewColumn,
163	        ])
164	        panes.orientation = .horizontal
165	        panes.alignment = .top
166	        panes.spacing = Self.gap
167	        panes.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight).isActive = true
168	
169	        messageLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
170	        messageLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
171	        messageLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = contentWidth
172	        messageLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.message")
173	
174	        insertButton.target = self
175	        insertButton.action = #selector(insertClicked(_:))
176	        insertButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.insert")
177	        fromFileButton.target = self
178	        fromFileButton.action = #selector(fromFileClicked(_:))
179	        fromFileButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.fromFile")
180	        exportButton.target = self
181	        exportButton.action = #selector(exportClicked(_:))
182	        exportButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.export")
183	        let cancelButton = sheetCancelButton(target: self, action: #selector(cancelClicked(_:)))
184	        cancelButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.cancel")
185	        view = makeSheetView(
186	            title: "Insert Graphic", content: sheetColumn([panes, messageLabel]),
187	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(
188	                cancel: cancelButton, apply: insertButton, leading: [exportButton, fromFileButton]),
189	            width: Self.width)
190	
191	        categoryTable.reloadData()
192	        if !categories.isEmpty {
193	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: 0), byExtendingSelection: false)
194	        }
195	        categoryChanged()
196	        chooseSelected()
197	    }
198	
199	    /// `select` chosen under This Project, then `message` shown (G-47 (f)).
200	    private func chooseSelected() {
201	        if let select = select,
202	            let section = categories.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == GraphicCatalog.thisProject }),
203	            let row = categories[section].items.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == select })
204	        {
205	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: section), byExtendingSelection: false)
206	            categoryChanged()
207	            graphicTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: row), byExtendingSelection: false)
208	            graphicChanged()
209	        }
210	        if let message = message { messageLabel.stringValue = message }
211	    }
212	
213	    private func configure(_ table: NSTableView, id: String) {
214	        let column = NSTableColumn(identifier: NSUserInterfaceItemIdentifier("name"))
215	        column.resizingMask = .autoresizingMask
216	        table.addTableColumn(column)
217	        table.headerView = nil
218	        table.rowHeight = 24
219	        table.style = .plain
220	        table.focusRingType = .none
221	        table.columnAutoresizingStyle = .firstColumnOnlyAutoresizingStyle
222	        table.dataSource = self
223	        table.delegate = self
224	        table.setAccessibilityIdentifier(id)
225	    }
226	
227	    private func scroll(_ table: NSTableView, width: CGFloat) -> NSScrollView {
228	        let scroll = NSScrollView()
229	        scroll.documentView = table
230	        scroll.hasVerticalScroller = true
231	        scroll.autohidesScrollers = true
232	        scroll.borderType = .lineBorder
233	        scroll.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
234	        scroll.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: width).isActive = true
235	        scroll.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight).isActive = true
236	        table.sizeLastColumnToFit()
237	        return scroll
238	    }
239	
240	    // MARK: - The two lists
241	
242	    private var chosenCategory: GraphicBrowserCategory? {
243	        let row = categoryTable.selectedRow
244	        return categories.indices.contains(row) ? categories[row] : nil
245	    }
246	
247	    private var chosenItem: GraphicBrowserItem? {
248	        let items = chosenCategory?.items ?? []
249	        let row = graphicTable.selectedRow
250	        return items.indices.contains(row) ? items[row] : nil
251	    }
252	
253	    func numberOfRows(in tableView: NSTableView) -> Int {
254	        tableView === categoryTable ? categories.count : (chosenCategory?.items.count ?? 0)
255	    }
256	
257	    func tableView(
258	        _ tableView: NSTableView, viewFor tableColumn: NSTableColumn?, row: Int
259	    ) -> NSView? {
260	        let cell = (tableView.makeView(withIdentifier: Self.cellID, owner: self)
261	            as? NSTableCellView) ?? Self.makeCell()
262	        if tableView === categoryTable {
263	            cell.textField?.stringValue = categories.indices.contains(row)
264	                ? categories[row].name : ""
265	            cell.textField?.textColor = DS.textStrong
266	        } else {
267	            let items = chosenCategory?.items ?? []
268	            let item = items.indices.contains(row) ? items[row] : nil
269	            cell.textField?.stringValue = item?.title ?? ""
270	            cell.textField?.textColor = item?.ok == false ? DS.textFaint : DS.textStrong
271	        }
272	        return cell
273	    }
274	
275	    func tableViewSelectionDidChange(_ notification: Notification) {
276	        if notification.object as? NSTableView === categoryTable {
277	            categoryChanged()
278	        } else {
279	            graphicChanged()
280	        }
281	    }
282	
283	    private static func makeCell() -> NSTableCellView {
284	        let cell = NSTableCellView()
285	        cell.identifier = cellID
286	        let field = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
287	        field.font = DS.sans(13)
288	        field.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
289	        field.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
290	        cell.addSubview(field)
291	        cell.textField = field
292	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
293	            field.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: cell.leadingAnchor, constant: 6),
294	            field.trailingAnchor.constraint(lessThanOrEqualTo: cell.trailingAnchor, constant: -6),
295	            field.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: cell.centerYAnchor),
296	        ])
297	        return cell
298	    }
299	
300	    /// A new category: its graphics listed, the first chosen.
301	    private func categoryChanged() {
302	        graphicTable.reloadData()
303	        if graphicTable.numberOfRows > 0 {
304	            graphicTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: 0), byExtendingSelection: false)
305	        }
306	        graphicChanged()
307	    }
308	
309	    /// A new graphic (or none): its title and description, Insert, and the
310	    /// preview playing it.
311	    private func graphicChanged() {
312	        let item = chosenItem
313	        titleLabel.stringValue = item?.title ?? ""
314	        descriptionLabel.stringValue = item?.description ?? ""
315	        descriptionLabel.toolTip = item?.description
316	        messageLabel.stringValue = ""
317	        insertButton.isEnabled = item != nil
318	        exportButton.isEnabled = item?.ok == true && !exporting
319	        if item == nil { previewView.image = nil }
320	        player.play(item.map(subject(for:)))
321	    }
322	
323	    /// What the preview draws `item` with: the template library's compile,
324	    /// or the document's registry for This Project.
325	    private func subject(for item: GraphicBrowserItem) -> GraphicPreviewPlayer.Subject {
326	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?
327	        switch item.origin {
328	        case .template:
329	            entry = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name)?.entry
330	        case .project:
331	            entry = document.flatMap {
332	                GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: item.name, for: $0.recipeKey)
333	            }
334	        }
335	        switch entry {
336	        case .compiled(let module, _, let meta, _)?:
337	            return .module(module, name: item.name, meta: meta)
338	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
339	            return .failed(name: item.name, diagnostics)
340	        case nil:
341	            return .failed(
342	                name: item.name, [.error("graphics/\(item.name).js is not compiled")])
343	        }
344	    }
345	
346	    private func showFrame(_ image: CGImage) {
347	        previewView.image = NSImage(
348	            cgImage: image, size: NSSize(width: image.width, height: image.height))
349	    }
350	
351	    // MARK: - Commit
352	
353	    @objc private func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
354	        dismiss(self)
355	    }
356	
357	    @objc private func fromFileClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
358	        fromFilePending = true
359	        dismiss(self)
360	    }
361	
362	    @objc private func graphicDoubleClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
363	        guard graphicTable.clickedRow >= 0, insertButton.isEnabled else { return }
364	        insertClicked(sender)
365	    }
366	
367	    /// The chosen graphic placed, once. A throw beeps and shows its sentence,
368	    /// and the sheet stays up; a success closes it.
369	    @objc private func insertClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
370	        guard let editor = editor, let item = chosenItem else {
371	            NSSound.beep()
372	            return
373	        }
374	        do {
375	            switch item.origin {
376	            case .template:
377	                guard let template = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name) else {
378	                    throw ReelCoreError(
379	                        message: "The template \"\(item.name)\" is not in this build's bundle")
380	                }
381	                try editor.insertGraphic(from: template.template.url, grouped: false)
382	            case .project:
383	                try editor.insertProjectGraphic(named: item.name, grouped: false)
384	            }
385	        } catch {
386	            NSSound.beep()
387	            messageLabel.stringValue = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message
388	                ?? error.localizedDescription
389	            return
390	        }
391	        dismiss(self)
392	    }
393	
394	    // MARK: - Export
395	
396	    /// The save panel, as a sheet on the browser, named `<module>.fjgraphic`.
397	    @objc private func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
398	        guard let item = chosenItem, item.ok, !exporting, let window = view.window else {
399	            NSSound.beep()
400	            return
401	        }
402	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
403	        panel.allowedContentTypes = [GraphicPackage.contentType]
404	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = "\(item.name).\(GraphicPackage.fileExtension)"
405	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
406	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
407	            self?.exportChosen(to: url)
408	        }
409	    }
410	
411	    /// The panel's OK (and the probe's entry): the chosen graphic's job built here, on main,
412	    /// and written on its own thread. A throw beeps and shows the sentence.
413	    func exportChosen(to url: URL) {
414	        guard let item = chosenItem, let document = document, !exporting else {
415	            NSSound.beep()
416	            return
417	        }
418	        let job: GraphicPackageJob
419	        do {
420	            switch item.origin {
421	            case .template:
422	                guard let template = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name) else {
423	                    throw ReelCoreError(
424	                        message: "The template \"\(item.name)\" is not in this build's bundle")
425	                }
426	                job = try GraphicPackageJob.template(template, document: document)
427	            case .project:
428	                job = try GraphicPackageJob.project(named: item.name, document: document)
429	            }
430	        } catch {
431	            NSSound.beep()
432	            messageLabel.stringValue = Self.sentence(error)
433	            return
434	        }
435	        exporting = true
436	        exportButton.isEnabled = false
437	        messageLabel.stringValue = "Exporting \(job.title)…"
438	        let thread = Thread { [weak self] in
439	            let outcome = Result { try job.write(to: url) }
440	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in self?.exportFinished(job, outcome) }
441	        }
442	        thread.stackSize = GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes
443	        thread.name = "com.kgalligan.framejob.graphic-export"
444	        exportThread = thread
445	        thread.start()
446	    }
447	
448	    private func exportFinished(
449	        _ job: GraphicPackageJob, _ outcome: Result<GraphicPackageResult, Error>
450	    ) {
451	        exporting = false
452	        exportButton.isEnabled = chosenItem?.ok == true
453	        switch outcome {
454	        case .success(let result):
455	            messageLabel.stringValue = "Exported \(job.title) to \(result.url.lastPathComponent): "
456	                + result.files.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
457	        case .failure(let error):
458	            NSSound.beep()
459	            messageLabel.stringValue = Self.sentence(error)
460	        }
461	    }
462	
463	    private static func sentence(_ error: Error) -> String {
464	        (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
465	    }
466	
467	    override func viewDidDisappear() {
468	        super.viewDidDisappear()
469	        player.stop()
470	        if fromFilePending {
471	            fromFilePending = false
472	            editor?.insertGraphicFromFile(nil)
473	        }
474	    }
475	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;

  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is

  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11

  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).

  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on

  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.

  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`

  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
